teaser: Finland's favorite painting comes with no explanation at all. The artist made sure of it.
review_notes:
Simberg refused to interpret the work; it is often said he first exhibited it with only a dash for a title (1903). Please confirm.
2006 Ateneum public vote: The Wounded Angel chosen as Finland's 'national painting'.
Simberg's illness (often given as meningitis) and stay at the Helsinki Deaconess Institute, autumn 1902 to spring 1903.
Setting: Eläintarha park and Töölönlahti bay, Helsinki; the path still exists; nearby institutions for the blind and disabled at the time.
Second, larger version painted as a fresco in Tampere Cathedral (then St John's Church), 1905-06.
Nightwish 'Amaranth' video (2007) is based on the painting.
Size about 127 x 154 cm.
Flowers identified as snowdrops, symbol of healing and rebirth.

lesson.text: Zero. That is the number of explanations Hugo Simberg gave for this painting. When it was first shown in Helsinki in 1903, he is said to have left the title line in the catalog as a simple dash. Asked what it meant, he answered that everyone should see in it what they wanted.

So start with what is plainly there. Two boys in heavy boots carry a stretcher made of two rough poles along a path. On it sits a girl in white with wings, head bowed. The land is bare and brown, early spring by the look of it, with cold water behind.

The scene is painted in the flat, careful manner you would use for a real event. Nobody glows. Nothing floats. Simberg treats an angel as a fact of rural life, and that deadpan tone is what makes the picture so strange. The injuries are painted just as soberly.

spots.title: The bandage
spots.text: A strip of white cloth is tied around her head and covers her eyes, knotted on top. She cannot see where she is being taken. Has she hurt her head, or her sight?

spots.title: Bare feet
spots.text: Her feet hang above the dirt while the boys tramp along in thick leather boots. She does not belong to this ground. She did not get here by walking.

spots.title: The grip
spots.text: Her left hand clamps the pole, knuckles up. She is weak but she is holding on by herself. This is not a body being carried away. It is a patient.

lesson.text: A patient is the right word. Simberg had just been one. From the autumn of 1902 to the spring of 1903 he lay in a Helsinki hospital with a severe illness, at times unsure he would recover. This canvas was the first large thing he finished afterward, and he had been sketching the idea for years before.

The place is real. The path runs through Eläintarha park beside Töölönlahti bay in Helsinki, and you can still walk it today. In Simberg's time it was a popular outing for working families, and it led past charitable institutions, including a school for blind girls.
There is one more injury, easier to miss than the bandage. It explains why she is on a stretcher at all.
An angel who cannot fly has a damaged wing. Find the blood.

spots.title: Blood on the wing
spots.text: A few red streaks stain the white feathers near the top of the wing. Simberg keeps the wound small and dry. He will not tell you whether she fell, or was struck.

lesson.text: Now the two bearers. They are dressed like country boys, but look at their clothes as colors: one entirely in black with a round hat, like a small undertaker, the other in brown. And they do not behave alike.

The boy in front keeps his eyes on the road. The one behind has turned his head and is staring directly out of the picture, at you. His expression is hard to bear: sullen, accusing, almost as if you were the one who did it. Every viewer gets caught by that look, and no one can say what he wants.

In 2006 the Ateneum museum asked Finns to vote for their national painting. The Wounded Angel won. A picture about injury and silent help beat every heroic landscape and every scene from the national epic.

Simberg loved it more than anything else he made. Two years later he was asked to decorate the new cathedral in Tampere, and he painted the angel and her bearers again, far bigger, as a fresco (a wall painting done on fresh plaster). Some churchgoers objected to his other murals there, which include a snake and a garden tended by skeletons.

spots.title: The stare
spots.text: The second boy's frown, aimed straight at you. He is the only figure who knows he is being watched.

spots.title: The boy in black
spots.text: Hat, jacket and trousers all black, face in profile and lowered. He walks like someone in a funeral procession.

spots.title: Snowdrops
spots.text: In her right hand she holds a small bunch of white flowers, usually identified as snowdrops, the first to bloom after winter. A quiet sign that recovery is possible.

spots.title: Ragged feathers
spots.text: The lower wing trails down past the stretcher, its edge frayed and uneven. The wings are heavy, real things that get in the way.

spots.title: The bay
spots.text: A band of pale water and a far shore under a gray sky. This is Töölönlahti, in the middle of Helsinki, painted with no city in sight.

spots.title: The signature
spots.text: Simberg signed and dated the canvas in the lower right corner, small and dark against the path.

lesson.text: The Finnish metal band Nightwish rebuilt the painting as a music video in 2007: two boys find a fallen angel and carry her home on a stretcher, while villagers decide she is a threat.

Is the angel innocence, hurt by the world? Is she Simberg himself, carried through his illness by others? Is the boy angry at us because we only watch? The painter kept his promise and never said. The dash where the title should be is still an invitation.

quiz.question: How did Simberg respond when asked what the painting meant?
options: He said viewers should see what they wanted in it
He said it showed a scene from the Bible
quiz.explanation: He refused to give any interpretation.

quiz.question: Where had Simberg spent the months before finishing the painting?
quiz.explanation: He was in a Helsinki hospital from autumn 1902 to spring 1903.

quiz.question: Which figure looks directly at the viewer?
options: The boy in front, dressed in black
The boy at the back, in brown
quiz.explanation: The second bearer turns his head and stares out of the picture.

quiz.question: What does the angel hold in her right hand?
options: A small bunch of white flowers
quiz.explanation: She holds snowdrops, the first flowers after winter.

quiz.question: What happened in 2006?
options: Finns voted it their national painting
It was moved to Tampere Cathedral
quiz.explanation: It won a public vote organized by the Ateneum museum.

facts.text: The landscape in the painting is an invented, imaginary place.
facts.explanation: It shows a real path by Töölönlahti bay in Helsinki that still exists.

facts.text: Simberg painted a second, larger version on the wall of Tampere Cathedral.
facts.explanation: He repeated the scene there as a fresco.

facts.text: The angel's wing is unharmed; only her eyes are injured.
facts.explanation: There are streaks of blood on the feathers of her wing.
